What? A completely reasonable response? Am I still sleeping? Kidding aside, I've been poking around the service this morning - it actually looks pretty interesting. Judging by my test upload, it appears my own playlist defaults to "Private". By keeping that setting on, would I still be at risk of copyright infringement by uploading my own (purchased) music collection? I was reading through the legal TOS and there's a lot in there regarding liability and copyright law.

Currently artists can attach themselves to their music to monetize it (among many other features).

Think of us as two services. One is a cloud hosting service for your music anywhere. Two is a searchable engine to discover and find two music/podcast/audio content.

Legally we have to follow the DMCA in regards of uploaded content to the cloud (we will adjust the copyright level of the song so it is not searchable).

However a goal of the site we don't want to circumvent artists/labels copyright, but find a better way for fans to connect to their music/playlists in a future setting. We make it easy for artists to sign up and control their copyright level of past, present, and future copyright. We want to work with artists to reach their fans.

Personally I think it is naive to think you can't type in any musical song into any search engine and find it. MiMx bridges this connection, beyond just YouTube (a video site), and will make the content deliver content more reliability and effectively to fans around the globe.

The default setting for your Song Library is private. However you can create other playlists that are non-private to share with other friends.

The site is still in a alpha state, but pretty polished as I code on it daily. Let me know if you have any suggestions to improve it.

In a nutshell, when users upload audio, they will always have personal access to it.

However, if an artist/label for whatever reason doesn't want that audio to be searchable to MiMx explore/search we adjust the copyright level so fans cannot find/search for it.
